security_cat_code_injection_why: Untrusted input can reach a code or template evaluation path, allowing arbitrary code execution in your runtime.
security_cat_prototype_pollution_why: Lets an attacker inject properties onto Object.prototype. Downstream code that reads those keys can be tricked into privilege escalation, logic corruption, or denial of service.
security_cat_ssrf_why: A crafted request can coerce the server into calling internal addresses — reaching cloud-metadata endpoints or internal services that should never be exposed.
security_cat_credential_leak_why: Authorization headers or secrets can be forwarded to an unintended origin during redirect handling, exposing them to third parties.
security_cat_header_injection_why: Unsanitized values written into request headers can poison downstream requests or exfiltrate data.
security_cat_csrf_why: A forged cross-origin request can perform state-changing actions on behalf of an authenticated user.
security_cat_redos_why: A malicious input string triggers catastrophic regex backtracking, pinning a CPU core and stalling the event loop for every request.
security_cat_dos_why: Unbounded resource consumption lets an attacker exhaust memory or CPU and take the service offline.
security_cat_null_byte_why: A null byte can truncate URL parsing, letting input slip past validation and reach unintended targets.
security_cat_other_why: A known security weakness in this dependency version.

virtual_users_tuned: Tuned for this product — overrides the disposition's {dials}
virtual_users_dial_reread: Re-reads before acting instead of trusting memory, {percent}% of the time
virtual_users_dial_repeat: Re-sends the call it just made, {percent}% of the time — the double-click
virtual_users_dial_empty_memory: Starts remembering nothing, whatever it is seeded with
virtual_users_dial_read_only: Never offered a call that changes anything
virtual_users_dial_inverted: A 2xx it should not have got is the finding, not a success
virtual_users_intents_note: It is handed this prose and nothing else — never the steps a scenario runs. Finding the API is the behaviour being tested.
virtual_users_reach_open: Open one to see which endpoints it counts.
virtual_users_nothing_to_want: Nothing to want: no scenario names {actor} and no goals are declared, so a run would stop where it started.
virtual_users_shows_everything: Shown the whole surface on purpose — for an adversarial user the grants are the oracle, not the filter.
virtual_users_withheld_approval: {count} held back: they need a human's approval
virtual_users_withheld_grants: {count} held back: outside the scopes this persona's roles confer
virtual_users_withheld_readonly: {count} held back: this one only reads
virtual_users_inferred: Read or write was guessed from the name for {count} of them
virtual_users_budget_default: Set per run with --steps, --mutations and --duration. Without any of them the engine stops after 40 steps.
virtual_users_run_note: Runs against a real stage, signing in as the actor over the app's own auth. A clean run proves nothing: it only means not this time, not with this seed.
virtual_users_disposition_realistic: Works towards its goal the way a competent user would: reads the schema, enters plausible values, finishes what it starts.
virtual_users_disposition_careless: Busy and distracted. Acts on what it half-remembers, submits twice when unsure, and enters odd-but-legal values. This is where most production bugs actually live.
virtual_users_disposition_newcomer: Has never seen the product. Starts with nothing remembered and has to discover everything, so anything only reachable if you already know it is unreachable.
virtual_users_disposition_stale: Comes back with old ids and old assumptions — some of what it remembers no longer exists.
virtual_users_disposition_auditor: Pursues no goal. Reads the same truth from several places and compares them, and is never offered a call that changes anything.
virtual_users_disposition_adversarial: Probes authorization and tenancy rather than pursuing a goal. It is shown the whole surface deliberately, and a 2xx from somewhere it is not entitled to is the finding.
virtual_users_disposition_accountable: Doing the job for real. What it changes stays changed, every call is recorded against its name, and it stops to ask rather than acting and reporting afterwards. The only disposition production accepts.
virtual_users_environments_default: Every configured environment except the production ones. Reaching production is opt-in: name it, and be accountable.
virtual_users_sync_note: Provisioning is separate from running: sync creates the account and applies the roles above. It is additive and never revokes.

surface_description: Everything Pikku gives you to import, in the order you meet it while building a service.
surface_select_item: Select an export to see where it comes from
surface_step_create_a_function: Everything starts as a function. It receives its data without knowing whether that arrived as a path param, a query string, a message body or a queue job, so nothing you write here has to be rewritten when the transport changes.
surface_step_enhance_it: Give it the things a function needs to be worth calling: typed errors it can throw, configuration it can read, and secrets and credentials it never has to hold itself.
surface_step_wire_it_up: Now decide how the outside world reaches it. Each wiring is one call, and a function can carry several — the same handler answering an HTTP route, a queue job and an MCP tool.
surface_step_guard_it: Say who may call it. Sessions come from auth, scopes gate the call outside the permission pool, and neither lives inside the function body.
surface_step_orchestrate_it: Compose functions into something longer-running: a workflow with durable steps and retries, or an agent that chooses which of them to call.
surface_step_test_it: Drive the whole thing the way a user would, in scenarios that run against a real server rather than a mocked one.
surface_unused: Nothing in this project imports it yet
surface_empty_description: The surface ships with @pikku/cli. Update it to a version that includes one, then reload.
